newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says anti-Cuba law based on security concerns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says anti-Cuba law based on security concerns.

text.p: The Unites States said on Thursday that a law aimed at discouraging foreign investment in Cuba was based on long-term U.S. security interests and was not an issue for the World Trade Organization.
State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said the United States was keeping open all options in dealing with the challenge to the Helms-Burton law in the WTO brought by the European Union.

"We have noted before that Helms-Burton and other laws are grounded in long-standing foreign policy and security concerns of the United States," Davies told reporters. "For these reasons we don't believe that they are the sorts of measures that should be placed in front of a trade panel."

The WTO agreed on Wednesday to a EU request for a dispute settlement panel to decide whether the Helms-Burton law violates international trade rules. The law allows U.S. citizens to sue foreign companies doing business with their property nationalized by Fidel Castro's Communist government.
The EU challenge was being backed by Mexico and Canada.

"We are confident that the Helms-Burton Act is fully consistent with our international trade obligations," Davies said. "And we don't think that yesterday's action by the European Commission should divert attention from the need for a more active approach to promoting democracy in Cuba."

Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat, who was assigned by President Bill Clinton the task of engaging other countries in bringing democracy to Cuba, has called the WTO challenge a "lose, lose" proposition that could play into the hands of protectionist forces in the United States.
The United States could invoke a national interest waiver to avoid abiding by an adverse WTO ruling.
But Eizenstat told reporters he hoped the dispute could be settled before a panel ruling.
"It's our belief that we won't have to face that case," Eizenstat said. "We hope that we will be able to resolve it."
